observations: Black PlayStation 4 console, original 'fat' model, wrapped in clear plastic film.
White DualShock 4 controller resting on the console.
Sony PlayStation logo visible on the top left of the console.
A small white sticker with handwritten numbers is on the top right.
Watermark 'KEVIN VIDEOS GAMES' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' on all photos.
All three photos show the same top-down perspective; no views of ports, labels, or the screen.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the System Information screen showing a firmware version at or below 11.00, or homebrew apps like GoldHEN.
Requires a photo of the console's dashboard/home screen showing the game icons.
No photos show the console powered on or connected to a display.

risks.risk: The console is not actually hacked (firmware is above 11.00).
risks.proof: Photo of Settings > System > System Information.

risks.risk: The console does not output video or has a damaged HDMI port.
risks.proof: Video of the console booting to the home screen on a TV.

risks.risk: The optical disc drive is faulty.
risks.proof: Video of a game disc being inserted and the game icon appearing.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive

risks.risk: The hard drive is the base 500GB rather than a larger upgrade.

proof_requests: Photo of the System Information screen showing the firmware version.
Photo of the home screen showing the 11 installed games.
Video of the console powered on and functioning on a TV screen.
Photo of the back of the console to check the HDMI port and model number sticker.
response.reason: The seller provides three identical photos of the console's exterior. There is no proof that the console works, is hacked, or contains the games mentioned. A 'hacked' status significantly changes the price but cannot be verified without seeing the system software version.
